content.title: About
content.content: Canned tomatoes are ripe red tomatoes that have been peeled, seeded, diced, and packed in glass or metal jars with tomato juice. They retain most of the flavor and nutrients of fresh tomatoes and are convenient for long‑term storage.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning allows tomatoes to be stored for 1–2 years without loss of taste.
Diced pieces are ideal for sauces, soups, and stews because they soften quickly.
Tomatoes are one of the most widely canned vegetables worldwide.
Lycopene and vitamin C are largely preserved during the canning process, though levels drop slightly.
Canned tomatoes often contain added salt and sometimes sugar to enhance flavor.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Contains vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A is essential for vision, skin health, and immune function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Tomatoes are a diet‑friendly food, providing volume with few calories.

items.title: Provides fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned tomatoes often contain added salt, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Bisphenol A (BPA)
items.content: Metal cans with certain linings can leach BPA; choose products in glass jars when possible.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Diced canned tomatoes are perfect for adding to sauces, soups, chili, stews, pizza, and salads. Use them as a base for tomato sauce or simply heat with herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the tomatoes in a sealed container in the refrigerator and use within 5–7 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors, mold, or color changes.
